dataPolicy: Public repository summary only. No large NGS data files are bundled into the portfolio.

thoughtProcess.title: Start from public sequencing data
thoughtProcess.body: Use SRA accession SRX9665373 and run SRR13233412 as the raw paired-end whole-genome sequencing source.

thoughtProcess.title: Prepare reads before variant work
thoughtProcess.body: Move raw reads through a preparation step so alignment and SNP search are reproducible.

thoughtProcess.title: Align and search for variants
thoughtProcess.body: Map the canine reads to a reference genome, then search for SNPs that can be investigated further.

thoughtProcess.title: Connect variants to genes
thoughtProcess.body: Translate candidate SNPs into gene-level context for canine degenerative myelopathy interpretation.

figures.title: Broad IGV locus view
figures.alt: IGV screenshot showing chromosome 31 from 26,658,238 to 26,660,830 with aligned sorted BAM reads.
figures.caption: The broad chromosome 31 window shows where the aligned read pileup sits inside the surrounding reference context. Sparse coverage is expected for low-coverage whole-genome sequencing, so the useful signal is concentrated in the local read stack rather than across the full interval.

figures.title: Candidate read support
figures.alt: IGV screenshot zoomed to chromosome 31 from 26,660,134 to 26,660,343 with several aligned reads and colored base mismatches.
figures.caption: The tighter window exposes individual reads spanning the candidate region. Colored bases within mostly green aligned reads mark mismatches or base-level differences to inspect before treating a position as a candidate SNP.

figures.title: Base-level variant inspection
figures.alt: IGV screenshot zoomed to chromosome 31 from 26,660,287 to 26,660,327 with reference bases and aligned reads visible.
figures.caption: At 40 bp resolution, the reference bases are visible above the alignments. The colored mismatches in the read track help identify exact positions that warrant downstream gene lookup and caution against overinterpreting unsupported single-read differences.
